library_preparation_preflight.agent_guidance: The library ships no concrete Repository implementation of its own (it's an abstraction layer consumed by store modules like spring-data-jpa/-mongodb). To exercise RepositoryFactorySupport and dynamic proxy creation, write a minimal in-memory concrete RepositoryFactorySupport/QueryLookupStrategy subclass in the test code itself, the same way spring-data-commons' own upstream test suite does, rather than depending on any store module. No environment variables or system properties are required.
risks: The coordinate org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-data-commons does not match any known Spring Boot artifact; spring-data-commons has historically been published under org.springframework.data, not org.springframework.boot. Worth confirming the correct groupId/artifactId before relying on this resolving at all — unrelated to the setup decision above.

spring-data-commons' ClassGeneratingEntityInstantiator generates accessor bytecode at runtime via cglib/Objenesis for fast entity instantiation; this is a native-image-sensitive mechanism worth watching during generation even though it doesn't change the setup decision here.

library_preparation_preflight.summary: spring-boot-data-commons is Spring Boot's shared autoconfiguration module (metrics instrumentation, Pageable/Sort web binding, generic repository support) with no binding to any datastore. The generated test exercises it entirely in-memory (fake ReactiveCrudRepository, SimpleMeterRegistry) with no real database, web server, or container. The existing build.gradle already declares the needed testImplementation deps (micrometer-core, reactor-core, assertj-core). No sibling spring-boot-data-* module in this repo (including the store-bound spring-boot-data-couchbase) requires a Docker image either, confirming this convention.
